acceptance: E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS responses (take and any other path that raises it) carry recovery steps that name the holding item, say that agents on this server share one worker identity, and give the supported ways forward: finish or release the claim, or run each concurrent agent on its own todo-db-mcp server with a distinct --actor
A test asserts the recovery text through the MCP envelope for the take path
The instructions text states the shared-identity consequence next to the E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS line

REVIEW 2026-10-28 against todo-db 0.10.1 (main d85cdf3), per the todo review checklist and review-protocol L2/L3. VERDICT: PARTLY VALID; narrowed. Verified: service.py raises E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS at the take and finish/renew claim checks through err(code, message), which sets no recovery. The original acceptance asked for two agents on one server to hold claims at once, and for one agent's claim to be protected from another agent without takeover. Both contradict ADR 0003 (one live claim per worker) and ADR 0006 G5 (instance-scoped worker), and are impossible without a per-agent identity on the wire; killed with that reason. The supported answer is separate servers with distinct --actor values, which this item now documents in the error.

TodoError and MutationOutcome carry an optional recovery list that _mutate passes into the envelope. Instructions and CHANGELOG updated. description: All agents that use one todo-db-mcp server share one worker identity, so one agent's live claim makes every other agent's take fail with E_MULTIPLE_CLAIMS. That identity model is deliberate (ADR 0003 section 2.3, ADR 0006 G5, and the get_instructions text 'One server instance is one logical worker'), but the error says only "worker 'X' already holds a live claim on 'Y'; release or finish it first" with an empty recovery list, so a subagent cannot tell that the holder is a sibling agent, not itself, or what to do. Seen as 12+ failed takes in one BenchBox session.
